about.title: About Us
about.headline: We believe early childhood is the foundation of the future
about.body1: Planet of the Free Child Nursery is a complete Montessori educational environment in Jeddah, founded with a clear vision: to give every child the opportunity to discover themselves and build their skills naturally and joyfully.
about.body2: We follow the globally trusted Maria Montessori methodology, where the child is at the center of the educational process, learning through free exploration, the senses, and interaction with a specially prepared environment.

curriculum.title: Five Areas of Learning
curriculum.subtitle: The Montessori curriculum is organised into five interconnected areas, each carefully designed to meet the natural developmental needs of the child. Together, they nurture the whole child — intellectually, physically, socially, and creatively.

practicalLife.title: Practical Life
practicalLife.desc: Practical Life activities encompass care of self, care of the environment, grace and courtesy, and control of movement — giving children the tools to act purposefully and independently in their everyday world. Through tasks such as pouring, buttoning, sweeping, and flower arranging, children develop deep concentration, fine motor precision, and a profound sense of order and belonging.
outcomes: Enhanced fine motor coordination and hand-eye precision
Growing independence in dressing, hygiene, and self-care routines
Internalised sense of order, sequence, and logical thinking
Respectful, courteous interactions with peers and adults

sensorial.title: Sensorial
sensorial.desc: Through a rich collection of specially designed Montessori materials, children systematically refine all five senses — sight, sound, touch, taste, and smell — and develop their capacity to observe, compare, and classify the world around them. The sensorial curriculum lays the cognitive groundwork for later abstract learning in mathematics, language, and the sciences by teaching children to notice subtle differences in dimension, colour, texture, pitch, and weight.
outcomes: Sharpened ability to observe and distinguish fine differences in the environment
Enriched vocabulary for describing qualities such as texture, weight, and pitch
Strengthened visual discrimination essential for reading and writing readiness
Foundation for abstract mathematical and scientific reasoning

language.title: Language & Literacy
language.desc: Language development at Planet of the Free Child begins long before pencil meets paper — through rich spoken language experiences, storytelling, poetry, and conversation that expand vocabulary and listening comprehension. Children then progress through Montessori's phonics-based approach to reading readiness, exploring sandpaper letters, the moveable alphabet, and phonetic reading materials, while simultaneous writing readiness is supported through metal insets and sandpaper letter tracing.
outcomes: Wide expressive and receptive vocabulary in Arabic and English
Confident phonemic awareness and phonics decoding skills
Early independent reading using phonetic and sight-word strategies
Clear, purposeful written expression through structured composition activities

mathematics.title: Mathematics
mathematics.desc: Montessori mathematics follows a concrete-to-abstract progression that allows children to physically feel quantity before ever encountering a symbol. Beginning with number rods and sandpaper numerals, children advance to the golden bead material for the decimal system, the stamp game, the bead chains, and ultimately abstract operations with large numbers — building genuine mathematical understanding rather than rote memorisation.
outcomes: Intuitive understanding of quantity, place value, and the decimal system
Confident performance of all four operations with concrete and symbolic materials
Strong number sense and early algebraic patterning awareness
Love of mathematical exploration and problem-solving confidence

cultural.title: Cultural Studies
cultural.desc: The Cultural area spans geography, botany, zoology, history, music, and art — inspiring children with a sense of wonder about the planet they inhabit and the living things they share it with. Through puzzle maps, timelines, nature specimens, and hands-on science experiments, children develop a global perspective, an appreciation for biodiversity, and a foundation in the arts that nourishes creativity and self-expression throughout life.
outcomes: Awareness of world continents, countries, and diverse human cultures
Foundational knowledge of plant and animal kingdoms through hands-on study
Understanding of historical time and the story of humanity
Creative expression through music, visual art, and movement

preparedEnvironment.title: The Prepared Environment
preparedEnvironment.desc: Every element of the Planet of the Free Child classroom is deliberately arranged to invite exploration and support independence. Materials are presented in a logical sequence on accessible, low shelves, allowing children to choose their own work and return it with care — building agency and responsibility alongside academic skills.

workCycle.title: The Uninterrupted Work Cycle
workCycle.desc: Children benefit from a three-hour uninterrupted work cycle each morning — a cornerstone of authentic Montessori practice. This extended period allows deep concentration to develop naturally, enabling children to enter a state of focused absorption known as 'normalisation', which Dr. Montessori identified as the hallmark of healthy development.

mixedAges.title: Mixed-Age Groupings
mixedAges.desc: Our classrooms bring together children across a three-year age span, mirroring the natural social structure of families and communities. Younger children learn by observing older peers, while older children deepen their own understanding through teaching — fostering empathy, leadership, and a collaborative community spirit.

autoeducation.title: Auto-Education
autoeducation.desc: Montessori believed that children possess within themselves an innate drive to learn. Our role is not to fill an empty vessel, but to prepare an environment rich enough to spark that inner teacher. Materials are self-correcting, so children receive immediate, non-judgmental feedback and develop the resilience to try again independently.

methodology.title: The Montessori Method in Practice
methodology.subtitle: Learning at Planet of the Free Child is never passive. Our educators act as guides, carefully observing each child and introducing new challenges at precisely the right moment — honouring every child's individual pace and learning style.

steps.title: Observation
steps.desc: Before any lesson is given, the Montessori guide observes each child closely — noting interests, readiness signals, and concentration patterns. This careful observation ensures that every presentation is offered at the ideal developmental window, making learning feel natural and effortless rather than forced.

steps.title: Presentation
steps.desc: The guide introduces a new material or concept through a precise, minimal three-period lesson. Movements are slow and deliberate, language is simple and purposeful, and the focus remains entirely on the material — inviting the child's curiosity without overwhelming it with unnecessary words or explanation.

steps.title: Independent Practice
steps.desc: After the presentation, the child freely chooses to work with the material as many times as they wish, at their own pace and on their own terms. Repetition is honoured as a sign of deep concentration, not boredom — it is through this self-directed repetition that true mastery is built from within.

steps.title: Mastery
steps.desc: Mastery is demonstrated not by a test, but by the child's calm, confident, and purposeful engagement with the material. The guide observes this readiness and records the achievement, then gently withdraws to allow consolidation before introducing the next extension in the sequence.

steps.title: Extension
steps.desc: Once mastery is achieved, the guide presents an extension activity that introduces greater complexity, abstraction, or a new application of the concept. Extensions keep the child in a state of productive challenge — neither bored by work that is too easy nor anxious about work that is too hard.

quote.text: The greatest sign of success for a teacher is to be able to say, 'The children are now working as if I did not exist.'
quote.author: Maria Montessori

dailyLife.badge: A Day at Planet of the Free Child
dailyLife.title: What a Day Looks Like
dailyLife.subtitle: Every day at Planet of the Free Child follows a warm, predictable rhythm that gives children a sense of security and belonging. Within this gentle structure, each child's day unfolds uniquely — guided by their own curiosity, energy, and readiness.

schedule.desc: Children arrive and are greeted individually by their guide. Morning routines such as hanging up bags, signing in at the attendance board, and choosing their first work of the day help children transition smoothly into the school environment and build a sense of ownership over their space.

The heart of the Montessori morning: a three-hour period of child-directed activity. Children move freely through the prepared environment, selecting materials from the five curriculum areas, working individually or in small groups, and engaging in lessons offered by the guide. Concentration deepens, and the classroom hums with purposeful, peaceful activity.

Children move to the outdoor environment for fresh air, physical exercise, and nature-based exploration. The outdoor space is an extension of the classroom — children may tend the garden, observe insects, participate in group games, or engage in imaginative play, all of which support physical development, risk assessment, and social negotiation skills.

Lunch is a social and practical life experience. Children set their own places, serve themselves where appropriate, practise mealtime conversation, and learn table manners within a warm, unhurried atmosphere. Cleaning up after eating reinforces responsibility and care for the shared environment.

Younger children rest in a cosy, darkened sleep area, while older children engage in quiet work, guided reading, journaling, or sensorial activities. Story time and music weave through this period, nurturing a love of literature, language, and calm self-regulation before the afternoon.

The afternoon is enriched with art, music, movement, cultural projects, and language sessions. Children reflect on their day, tidy their materials, and prepare for dismissal. Guides share brief observations with families at pick-up, keeping parents connected to their child's daily journey and achievements.

environment.title: Our Prepared Environment
environment.desc: The Planet of the Free Child classroom is designed to be a third teacher — every surface, shelf, and corner thoughtfully arranged to support independence, beauty, and purposeful work. We draw on principles of calm aesthetics, natural materials, and child-proportioned furniture to create a space where children feel genuinely at home and intrinsically motivated to explore.
features: Low, open shelves that place every material within a child's reach and field of vision
Abundant natural light and carefully chosen neutral tones that promote calm and focus
Child-sized furniture — tables, chairs, and trolleys — scaled precisely to each age group
Uncluttered, orderly spaces where each material has a defined home and purpose
Materials arranged in sequential order from simple to complex, left to right on each shelf
